text:
Maria (Research): sharing draft cost-vs-quality scorecard for the new model family. gdoc: https://go.redwood/doc/model-cost-quality (please comment). TL;DR at the bottom.

Lee (ML Eng): ran quantization sweep on 13B and 7B variants. quick summary: q4 gives ~60% cost reduction vs fp16, quality drop small for helpfulness/truthfulness.

eval-bot: automated eval summary attached. (See block)

```
Model                      | Helpfulness | Truthfulness | Avg latency p50 | p95 latency | Cost / 1k tok
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Redwood-13B-fp16 (baseline)| 89.1        | 95.0         | 120ms           | 420ms      | $0.045
Redwood-13B-q4            | 87.4        | 94.2         | 130ms           | 480ms      | $0.018
Redwood-7B-q4             | 85.6        | 92.0         | 95ms            | 360ms      | $0.012
Redwood-13B-q4+kv-cache    | 88.0        | 94.3         | 95ms (amortized) | 300ms     | $0.010 (effective)
```

AJ (Product): 2 quick q's — how do you measure "helpfulness"? and what is the user-visible regression risk?

Maria (Research): helpfulness = human eval (n=1k prompts, pairwise preference head-to-head vs baseline). regression risk: low for short QA but slightly higher on multi-step reasoning prompts (we saw a 2.1 pt drop).

Lee (ML Eng): additional notes:
- quantization config: `q4_0` with per-channel scales for attention and linear ops.
- failure modes: occasional tokenization artifacts on long tails, fixable via LM head rewrites.
- we instrumented eval set to track hallucination rate and semantic answer F1. Hallucination +0.6% vs baseline on reasoning set.

Sam (Infra): memory / infra implications:
- Redwood-13B-fp16 needs 48GB for stable KV cache + batch.
- 13B-q4 fits on 32GB with room for caching.
- p99 latency increases ~10-15% on q4 due to dequant/requant overhead.

Hana (SRE): monitoring + rollback plan:
- require drift alerts on helpfulness and hallucination (daily eval).
- can do canary rollout to 5% traffic for 24h; if helpfulness delta < 1.5 and hallucination delta < 1.0%, proceed.
- fallback: route to baseline fp16 or smaller model pool.

Nate (GTM): messaging question — if we switch to q4 default for Hosted API, what do we tell customers re: SLA and quality?

Maria (Research): suggested guidance for product/GTN:
- Default recommendation: Redwood-13B-q4 as cost-default for general chat/search workloads where latency/cost matter and extreme reasoning is not primary.
- Opt-in: `high_quality=true` to pin fp16 baseline for customers who want max quality (enterprise tier).
- Show cost/quality toggle in Console with clear unit economics: "Projected savings vs baseline" and "Measured quality delta".

Lee (ML Eng): recommendation matrix (short):
- Use 13B-q4 for web search/chat assistants (good help/truth balance, 60% cost savings).
- Use 7B-q4 for high throughput low-cost tasks (embeddings-ish use cases or lightweight assistants) with explicit warnings about reasoning degradation.
- Reserve fp16 for evaluation, critical reasoning flows, and paid enterprise tier.

AJ (Product): ok, can we get a one-slide summary for PM org + one for GTM that includes: cost per 1k tokens, expected quality delta, recommended rollout plan?

Maria (Research): yes, I'll produce both. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Lee (ML Eng): practical ops to ship:
- add quantized model variants to model catalog with `compat_fallback` tags.
- add canary route in Smart Routing (5/25/50).
- add automated daily eval job in CI that posts to #model-regressions.

Sam (Infra): I'll validate GPU memory profiles on Dedicated pools and run soak tests for 48h.

Hana (SRE): I'll draft alert thresholds and playbook for rollback.

Nate (GTM): I'll draft customer messaging and pricing blurb (savings examples).

Maria (Research): final note — unit economics example: swapping baseline to 13B-q4 reduces token cost from $0.045 to $0.018 => at 50M tokens/month that's ~$1.35k -> $0.9k savings monthly per heavy account (~33% infra cost reduction). exact savings depend on caching and batching.

Lee (ML Eng): also callout: enabling KV cache + async batching can further reduce effective cost to ~$0.010 per 1k tokens on steady state workloads.

AJ (Product): love it. let's aim for canary next week. please ping me when slide deck is ready. :thumbsup:

Maria (Research): thanks all — will post the slide drafts and the full gdoc with eval artifacts. ping @AJ (Product) for review.
